title: First Congress of the Peoples of the East, Baku
summary: The Communist International convened a congress in Baku in September 1920 for delegates from Asia and the Middle East. Nearly 1,900 delegates attended, and the gathering issued a manifesto urging workers and peasants of the East to unite with European workers against imperialism, especially British. Historians treat it as an early Comintern effort to reach colonised peoples.

uncertainty.note: Sources agree on 1 September for the opening; 8 September for the close is from the Slavic Review abstract.

as_recorded.value: held in Baku from September 1 to 8, 1920
On September 1, 1920, in the city of Baku

importance.justification: An early international gathering linking the Comintern to anti-colonial and revolutionary movements across Asia.

sources.title: Baku Congress of the Peoples of the East: Manifesto

reviewer_note: Delegate counts vary by source (1,891 in the stenographic protocol; about 1,900 to over 2,000 elsewhere), so the summary says nearly 1,900. The Comintern summons is attested by a Marxists.org foreword, not opened in full here.
